drivingQuestion: From where do we know the maidservant case?

segments.en: gemara The mishna teaches that «one who engages in intercourse with» an espoused «maidservant» brings an offering for an intentional transgression as he does for an unwitting transgression. The Gemara asks: «From where do we» derive this?

segments.he: דְּתָנוּ רַבָּנַן: ״וְכִפֶּר עָלָיו הַכֹּהֵן בְּאֵיל הָאָשָׁם עַל חַטָּאתוֹ אֲשֶׁר חָטָא״, מְלַמֵּד שֶׁמֵּבִיא קׇרְבָּן אֶחָד עַל עֲבֵירוֹת הַרְבֵּה. ״בְּאֵיל הָאָשָׁם... וְנִסְלַח לוֹ מֵחַטָּאתוֹ אֲשֶׁר חָטָא״ – לַעֲשׂוֹת שׁוֹגֵג כְּמֵזִיד.
segments.en: «As the Sages taught» in a baraita: The verse states: «“And the priest shall make atonement for him with the ram of the guilt offering» before the Lord «for his sin that he has sinned”» (Leviticus 19:22). The superfluous phrase: That he has sinned, «teaches that» he «brings one offering for several transgressions.» Furthermore, the verse concludes: «“With the ram of the guilt offering» before the Lord for his sin that he has sinned; «and he shall be forgiven for his sin that he has sinned.”» The second occurrence of the phrase “that he has sinned” serves «to render» the halakha with regard to «an unwitting» transgression the same «as» it is with regard to «an intentional» transgression, that one brings a guilt offering in either case.

moves.summary: Source for the mishna's maidservant clause?

edges.about: source that one who lies with a designated maidservant brings an offering even for intentional sin
the doubled 'that he sinned' equates unwitting and intentional
the doubled phrasing teaches one offering for many sins and equates unwitting with intentional
